purpose: The core case: a candidate who meets every required qualification and misses most preferred ones. Carries the five content traps seen on a real run — a finished degree read as ongoing, listed skills reported missing, an absolute 'no metrics' claim, an either/or language requirement read as a gap, and LaTeX accent artifacts the ATS section must flag.

mustMatch.why: The CV text carries LaTeX extraction artifacts (Jos´e, Ingenier´ıa). The real run caught these; it must not regress. The artifact character itself is deliberately not in the pattern: quoting it as evidence is not the same as naming the problem.

mustNotMatch.why: Both degrees ended before today (March 2025 and 2021). Calling one ongoing is a temporal error. The "ongoing" branch ignores any pairing that names both states - "ongoing or completed", "completed or ongoing", "ongoing or recently finished" - because naming both asserts neither. Each spelling cost a correct run a failure before it was allowed for.

mustNotMatch.pattern: (?<!\b(?:most|many|some|several|few|others?|remaining|majority|almost all|nearly all|rest)\b[^.]{0,40})(?<!\b(?:sections?|roles?|positions?|entries|entry|listings?|bullets?|bullet points?|descriptions?|projects?|summary|job)\b[^.]{0,45})(?:absence of|devoid of|not a single|zero|completely lacks?|entirely lacks?|totally lacks?|lacks?|lacking|no|without)\s+(any\s+|explicit\s+|clear\s+)?(?:quantif|quantitat|measurable|metric|concrete number|figures?|percentages?)(?![^.]{0,60}\b(?:in|across|for|from|beyond|outside)\s+(?:the\s+)?(?:most|many|some|several|few|others?|remaining|majority|almost all|nearly all|rest)\b)
mustNotMatch.why: FAILURE 5: the resume contains a quantified achievement, so an unqualified claim that metrics are absent is false. Three guards keep it fair, each added after a correct run was scored as a failure: a hedge before the claim ("most bullets lack metrics"), a hedge after it ("lacks metrics in almost all bullets"), and a named part of the resume as the subject ("Project descriptions lack quantitative validation"), which is a claim about that part and can be true while the resume as a whole has a figure. A genuine absolute names the resume, the text or the work history, or has no subject at all. Read it together with the positive assertion on quantifiedAchievements, which is the authoritative one.

requirements.why: FAILURE 2: every one of these is in the CV's own skills section. Under the M2c-F shape this is a requirements assertion: an entry naming only this term may not be "missing", since the CV has it.
FAILURE 7: the posting lists these languages as alternatives, and the CV has some of them, so none of the rest is a requirement of its own.
